key_insight: For semilinear parabolic PDEs, neural approximation costs separate into governing-law complexity and data encoding, explaining why compact networks can approximate infinite-dimensional solution operators.
engineering_relevance: Exploiting PDE structure can yield compact surrogate architectures whose parameter costs do not grow with grid resolution or time-step refinement.
method: Represent the constitutive law with a neural block whose approximation cost depends on its computation graph.
Encode input data using a bounded number of learned weights per mode.
Derive trajectory-level approximation bounds and near-matching lower bounds for viscous Hamilton–Jacobi equations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees rather than numerical evaluations: logarithmic nonlinear-block cost for 2D Navier–Stokes and approximately η^(-1/s) parameters for viscous Hamilton–Jacobi equations, with a matching lower bound up to logarithms.
watch_item: Approximation guarantees do not establish that practical training will find the predicted compact networks.
paper_title: Neural Network Approximation and Structural Complexity of Semilinear PDEs with Lower Bounds
